_about: Places of legend with no location of their own, placed where tradition or a scholar puts them; each a claim, with the Wikipedia article it comes from (read 2026-10-21).

places.name: Avalon (Glastonbury Tor)
places.claim: Since the 12th century Glastonbury has been identified with the isle of Avalon, where King Arthur was taken after his last battle.

places.name: Lyonesse
places.claim: In Arthurian legend, the country of Tristan, said to have sunk beneath the sea between Land's End and the Isles of Scilly.

places.name: Cantre'r Gwaelod
places.claim: A legendary sunken kingdom in Cardigan Bay, drowned when the sluice gates were left open; the drowned forest at Borth is pointed to as its remains.

places.name: Camelot? (Cadbury Castle)
places.claim: John Leland in 1542 named the hillfort of Cadbury Castle as Camelot, King Arthur's court.

places.name: Camelot? (Caerleon)
places.claim: Geoffrey of Monmouth made the Roman town of Caerleon the seat of Arthur's court; later writers linked it with Camelot.

places.name: Camelot? (Winchester)
places.claim: Thomas Malory identified Camelot with Winchester, where the 13th-century Round Table hangs in the Great Hall.
